name: X-linked Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for X-linked Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutation in the causative gene on the X chromosome
Progressive cerebellar ataxia with gait disturbance and limb incoordination
Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern
Exclusion of other causes of spinocerebellar ataxia by clinical and laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive cerebellar ataxia plus genetic confirmation of pathogenic mutation on the X chromosome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis due to phenotypic overlap with other ataxias.

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic and inflammatory causes of ataxia
imaging: MRI showing cerebellar atrophy predominantly affecting the vermis and hemispheres
genetic: Pathogenic mutation in the gene located on the X chromosome associated with spinocerebellar ataxia type 3
other: Nerve conduction studies demonstrating sensory and motor axonal neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: CAG trinucleotide repeat expansions in ATXN3 gene
Later onset and different genetic locus
GAA repeat expansions in FXN gene

redFlags: Rapid progression of ataxia over weeks
Early onset with severe cognitive decline
Presence of systemic features suggesting alternative diagnosis
references: Orphanet: X-linked Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3 - ORPHA:85297
Recent review articles on X-linked cerebellar ataxias
